verses.text: This happened in the days of Ahasuerus, the Ahasuerus who ruled 127 provinces from India all the way to Ethiopia.
At the time, King Ahasuerus ruled from his royal throne in the palace at Susa.
In his third year as king, he threw a feast for all his officials and servants. The army of Persia and Media was there, along with the nobles and provincial leaders.
For a full 180 days, he showed off the wealth of his glorious kingdom and the splendor of his royal majesty.
When those days were over, the king threw a seven-day feast in the courtyard of his palace garden. Everyone at the palace in Susa was invited, from the most important to the least.
White and blue hangings were tied with fine linen and purple cords to silver rings and marble pillars. Gold and silver couches stood on a floor of red, white, yellow, and black marble.
Drinks came in gold cups of all kinds. There was plenty of royal wine, thanks to the king’s generosity.
Under the rules, no one had to drink. The king had told all his household officials to let each guest decide for himself.
Queen Vashti also threw a feast for the women in King Ahasuerus’s royal house.
On the seventh day, when the wine had put the king in high spirits, he gave an order to Mehuman, Biztha, Harbona, Bigtha, Abagtha, Zethar, and Carcass, the seven eunuchs who served him in person.
He told them to bring Queen Vashti before him wearing her royal crown. She was beautiful, and he wanted to show off her beauty to the people and the officials.
But Queen Vashti refused to come when the eunuchs brought the king’s order. The king was furious. His anger burned inside him.
The king turned to the wise men who understood the times. It was his custom to consult those who knew the law and how to judge a case.

The men closest to him were Carshena, Shethar, Admatha, Tarshish, Meres, Marsena, and Memucan, the seven leaders of Persia and Media who had access to the king and held the highest places in the kingdom.
The king asked, “Under the law, what should we do about Queen Vashti? She didn’t obey the order King Ahasuerus sent through the eunuchs.”
Memucan answered in front of the king and his officials, “Queen Vashti has wronged more than the king. She’s wronged all the officials and everyone in every province of King Ahasuerus.

Women everywhere will hear what the queen did. When the word gets around that ‘King Ahasuerus ordered Queen Vashti to be brought before him, but she wouldn’t come,’ they’ll look down on their husbands.
Today the noblewomen of Persia and Media who’ve heard what the queen did will tell it to all the king’s officials. It’ll lead to plenty of contempt and anger.

“If it pleases the king, issue a royal order and write it into the laws of Persia and Media so it can’t be changed. Let Vashti never come before King Ahasuerus again, and let the king give her royal position to someone better than she is.
When the king’s order goes out across his whole kingdom, vast as it is, wives everywhere will honor their husbands, whoever they are.”
The king and his officials liked the advice, so the king did what Memucan suggested.
He sent letters to every province, using each province’s script and each people’s language. The order said every man was to rule his own household and speak the language of his own people.
